blocks.title: Acid rain
blocks.text: Precipitation (rain, snow, sleet or hail) with a pH below about 5 to 6 is acid rain.

Burning fossil fuels releases SOx and NOx into the atmosphere; these gases mix with moisture to form acids, and wind can carry the acidic droplets huge distances before they return to the ground as acid rain, hail, snow or even fog. Acid rain looks, feels and tastes like clean rain, but its corrosive nature causes widespread damage to the environment. The key reactions: SO2 from fossil fuels is oxidised to SO3, 2SO2(g) + O2(g) gives 2SO3(g), which reacts with water to give sulfuric acid, SO3(g) + H2O(l) gives H2SO4(aq); nitrogen oxide reacts with water to give nitric and nitrous acids, 2NO2 + H2O gives HNO3 + HNO2.
What are the main chemical processes in the formation of acid rain, and write the balanced equation with state symbols for sulfuric acid from atmospheric sulfur trioxide.
